Welcome—I'm so glad you're here. Have you ever noticed how the news seems filled with alarming headlines and bleak predictions? It's easy to feel overwhelmed, or even a bit hopeless, about the state of the world. But what if I told you that behind all those headlines, a story of progress is quietly unfolding—one that's often missed?
Together, we're about to explore the big ideas inside Hans Rosling’s eye-opening book, Factfulness: Ten Reasons We're Wrong About the World – and Why Things Are Better Than You Think. Rosling invites us to step back, challenge our assumptions, and see the world through a fresh, evidence-based lens.
You and I are going to dig into the instincts that shape how we see global trends—like that nagging sense of fear or the urge to split everything into good and bad. These instincts might make us miss the incredible improvements happening every day in health, education, and prosperity across the planet.
We'll travel through vivid stories and surprising data, looking at ten powerful instincts that can cloud judgment and lead us to underestimate just how far the world has come. This isn’t just about numbers—it's about learning how our minds work, and how we can spot hope and progress, even while facing real challenges.
By questioning old beliefs and embracing a fact-based worldview, we’ll discover a new sense of hope and possibility. So, let’s get curious together. Let’s open our minds to a deeper appreciation of the world’s complexity—and its tremendous promise.
